question: If you want to save a workbook in MS Excel 365 so that only viewing is allowed and editing is restricted, which feature should you use?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Read-Only Mode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Read-Only Mode** in MS Excel allows users to open and view a workbook while restricting editing and modifications.
 
• This feature is useful for sharing sensitive data that needs to be protected from unauthorized changes.
 
• To enable Read-Only Mode, you can save the workbook and select the **"Tools > General Options"** in the Save As dialog box, then set a password for editing.
 
• Users can view the file without entering the password, but they cannot make changes unless they have the editing password.
 
• Read-Only Mode ensures data integrity and helps prevent accidental or intentional modifications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protected View:**

 
 
• Files opened from potentially unsafe locations (e.g., email attachments) are opened in Protected View to prevent malicious content from affecting your system.
 
• Protected View allows viewing but blocks editing until explicitly enabled by the user.
 
 
 
• **Workbook Password Protection:**
 
 
• Excel allows users to set passwords to restrict access to the workbook or worksheet.
 
• Passwords can be set for opening and/or editing the file.
 
 
 
• **Track Changes Feature:**
 
 
• Excel provides the "Track Changes" feature to monitor modifications made to a workbook collaboratively.
 
• It helps identify who made edits and what changes were made.
 
 
 
• **Freeze Panes:**
 
 
• This feature is used to lock specific rows or columns while scrolling through a worksheet.
 
• It enhances visibility but does not provide security or restrict editing.
